title: Drummers supporting soloists and jumping the gun
summary: Greene says drummers should back the soloist, accent brass figures on time, and not rush ahead of the beat.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Would you say that guys, -- drummers today recognize their responsibility to soloists like they used to? Do you think drummers -- that they realize that what they're supposed to be doing is backing a guy up? Falling in behind a guy the way he feels?
I don't know. I really don't know whether they realize this fact or not.
Because, I mean, that's what anybody in the band asks of the drummer.
Right.
That's all that you ask of the drummer is support.
Right. Support. Alot of drummers don't want to support. They want to --
Sure.
They want to shine, you know.
Yeah.
Okay -- when your time comes, go ahead. That's the only fault I have. When it's your turn, then do your thing. But, when someone else is doing it, I mean, you support him.
Well, that's -- but I mean -- that's a whole large question that you go back thirty years to the beginning of bebop when the drummers are no longer -- I mean they're doing solo at the same
time as the saxophones. So, I mean, you've got to argue all that out.
Yeah. Yes, I know.

But, the only thing -- you know, what you were saying there, Freddie -- you know -- breaks, and filling in the holes in arrangements, but when they started to accent the figures in the arrangement -- the brass for example -- well, this is where I think they also began to go wrong, because then you're so damn busy, you know, accenting what the horns are playing.
Yeah. I don't mind that too much, personally, if they are accented right.
Right.
But, sometimes they jump the gun.
That's right.
If they're right on time with the brass -- alright.
Yeah.

Most drummers -- they want to be first. Instead of saying 'bam' they say 'bam' (ahead of beat). You know what I mean. And, when they do that they can't come back where they left. Because they jump the gun, and they stay out there. You see, if they say 'bam' (on beat) -- okay. But, if they say 'bam' (ahead of beat) -- that's a different tempo.
In other words they're going to stay ahead right through.
Right. Yeah. It's alright if they jump (laugh) and then jump back.
Yeah.
You know what I mean. That's really not alright, but, if they're able to jump out there and then come on back --
In other words, to correct their error.
Right. But, some of them have a heck of a time getting back. And, sometimes they stay out there and they think they're right and they just, you know --
Well, Freddie, so, I mean, now when there's a little conflict like this, now -- then does Basie put his eye on the drummer?
Well, he has to recognize it.
He does?
Oh, yeah. He will recognize it. Has to. (laugh)
Yeah, I know he does. Does he let the guy know he does?
(laugh) I think so. I think he'll either open an eye or something like that. Look at him, and then he'll probably realize what's going on.
Yeah. Yeah. Catch himself.
